Issued at 253 PM EST Tue Nov 24 2026

Now through Friday Night...

Afternoon weather conditions across the region were mostly sunny 
with temperatures in the 45-50 degree range.  For the remainder of 
the afternoon, no significant weather is expected and highs will top 
out in the 45-50 degree range.  Temps will cool into the upper 
30s/40s by mid evening.  

For tonight, clouds will be on the increase across the region with a 
continued southerly flow.  The blended guidance appeared too cold 
and coordinating with surrounding offices, we went closer to the 
CONSShort dataset which will result in overnight lows in the lower-
middle 30s.  After midnight, isentropic lift ahead of an approaching 
wave will lead to some light rain showers lifting northward across 
the central and western KY.  As this precipitation crosses the Ohio 
River toward dawn, a few valley locations in southern IN may briefly 
dip below 32 and there may be a very brief period of sleet/freezing 
rain.  However, temperatures are expected to rapidly rise after 
sunrise.

Moving into Wednesday and Thanksgiving Day, we'll be watching a 
closed low drop southward out of the Midwest while a weaker 
shortwave trough axis moves out of the Red River Valley.  The global 
models are still trying to resolve whether these two features will 
phase.  The GFS/GEM solutions continue to phase the systems, but the 
more reliable Euro doesn't phase these systems and the closed upper 
low simply drops southward into the TN Valley while a resulting 
surface cyclone moves northward along the eastern US coast.  Cold 
air associated with the upper level low will drop into IL/MO 
resulting in a band of heavy snow along the MS River.

Locally, we'll see a brief lull in precipitation from late Wednesday 
morning and into the afternoon.  Highs on Wednesday will range from 
45-50 west of I-65 and 50-55 east of I-65.  Lows Wednesday night 
will be the middle-upper 30s.  Widespread rain showers will persist 
into the day on Thursday with highs in the 45-50 degree range and 
gusty winds of 25-30 mph at times.  As we move into Thursday 
afternoon and evening, colder air aloft will spread into the region 
from the west/southwest as the aforementioned upper low moves into 
the TN Valley.  The track of the upper low will be critical into who 
sees a rain/snow mix or perhaps a period of pure snow with this 
system.  The GFS/GEM have a more slightly northward track allowing 
for precip to fall a mix of rain/snow across much of central KY. The 
Euro is further south and would keep much of the rain/snow mix 
across far southern KY and into middle TN.  Looking at soundings, 
thermal profiles will be near critical thresholds so the usual 10:1 
snow ratio isn't going to hold here.  More likely ratios would be on 
the order of 5-6:1.  Also in this case, the p-type may end being 
modulated by precipitation intensity, in other words, heavier precip 
may end up falling as rain/snow or pure snow for a time, while 
lighter precipitation may end up as all rain.  For now, we'll carry 
a mix of rain/snow showers in the forecast for late Thursday and 
into Friday morning.  With low temperatures expected to remain above 
freezing Thursday night, very minor snowfall accumulations will be 
possible and limited to elevated objects and grassy surfaces. 
Depending on the track of the upper low, this portion of the 
forecast may need further refinement over the next few forecast 
cycles.

The upper low will move east of the region on Friday, but northwest 
flow and plentiful moisture will result in showery conditions on 
Friday with a drying trend into the afternoon/evening.  Highs on 
Friday will be in the low-mid 40s with overnight lows dropping into 
the upper 20s.

Saturday through Tuesday...

Upper flow looks to relax and become more zonal as we get into 
Saturday with partly to mostly sunny skies and temperatures warming 
into the 53-58 degree range.  Overnight lows will be in the mid-
upper 30s.

Progressive flow aloft will send another fairly strong shortwave 
trough into the region by Sunday.  Model soundings are not overly 
unstable here, but lapse rates steepen a bit and showers and few 
thunderstorms may be possible, though the best combo of 
forcing/moisture for thunderstorms looks to be more concentrated 
over far western KY/southern IL.  After that system passes, a drier 
period of weather looks likely for Monday/Tuesday.  Highs here will 
be in the mid-upper 50s with lows in the 30s.
